BudgetWise: ASP.NET Core Web API (.NET 8) + React TypeScript/Vite/Tailwind personal-finance training app.

C#: PascalCase types/methods/properties; camelCase locals/parameters; meaningful names; focused methods/SRP; composition over inheritance; C# 12 where appropriate; `var` when obvious; usings inside namespaces; constructor-parameter DI; appropriate Scoped/Singleton/Transient lifetimes; minimal APIs or controllers consistently; nullable references; property initialization; `required` mandatory properties. Services contain business logic. DTOs (immutable `record`s) separate request/response; explicit domain mapping; Data Annotations/FluentValidation; camelCase JSON; proper Content-Type/status codes and meaningful errors; REST nouns/plural resources, HTTP actions, `/api/expenses/{id}`, query filtering; typed results/`IActionResult`; middleware for authentication/CORS; navigation properties; in-memory realistic `MockData` in `Data/MockData.cs`.

React/TS: strict TypeScript; no inline styles; Tailwind utilities; hooks/functional, focused reusable components; semantic accessible HTML, ARIA and keyboard navigation; no render side effects; JSDoc. Keep code clear, simple, beginner-friendly; explain WHY in comments; XML docs (`<summary>`, `<param>`, `<returns>`, `<exception>`) for public APIs; `// TODO:` descriptions; follow existing patterns, .NET/React conventions, error handling, validation, typed responses, full-stack coherence; tests/docs for features and TODOs.

Testing: xUnit, React Testing Library, AAA, descriptive `MethodName_WhenCondition_ThenExpectedResult`; `WebApplicationFactory<T>` integration; mock external dependencies/API (MSW); success/failure, edge/boundary, accessibility and user interactions.

❌ Do not use service locator pattern (always use dependency injection)
❌ Do not return null from API endpoints (use `NotFound()` or throw exceptions)
❌ Do not put business logic in controllers (use services)
❌ Do not ignore exceptions or use empty catch blocks
